## Otis Modernization Projects at Willis Tower and Shanghai Science Museum Win Elevator World Awards


11/24/2026


Download (opens in new window)


- Award-winning projects demonstrate complex modernization at two globally recognized destinations


FARMINGTON, Conn.


, Nov. 24, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Elevator World magazine has selected two[Otis Worldwide Corporation](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4830168-1&h=543207046&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.otis.com%2Fen%2Fcompany&a=Otis+Worldwide+Corporation) (NYSE: **OTIS** ) modernization projects as winners in its annual Project of the Year awards. Otis is the world's leading elevator and escalator manufacturing, installation, service and modernization company.


Willis Tower in Chicago won in the Elevators Modernization category and Shanghai Science and Technology Museum received the honor in the Escalators Modernization category. The two very different modernization projects demonstrate the scale and range of Otis modernization expertise: one at a globally recognized supertall building and the other at a major public museum where mobility technology becomes an integral part of how people explore the building.


"Modernization and refurbishment is about more than upgrading equipment. It's about understanding what our customers need and bringing the full strength of Otis to solve their most complex challenges," said Judy Marks, Otis Chair, CEO & President. "At Willis Tower, our teams took on extraordinary scale and complexity while keeping this landmark building in operation. At the Shanghai Science and Technology Museum, we brought together modern equipment and digital technology in a way that enhances the visitor experience. These awards are a great recognition of what our teams can accomplish through engineering expertise, innovation, and close customer collaboration." The projects will be featured among other winners in Elevator World's January 2027 edition.


**Why Willis Tower won Elevator Modernization of the Year**


Completed more than 50 years after the iconic building first opened, the project replaced an aging elevator system with a modern, connected transportation system designed to improve reliability, passenger flow and long-term performance.


At the same time, it helped support a broader transformation of the supertall property and maintain its status as a world-class visitor attraction.


Beginning in 2017, and with Otis officially turning over the final elevator in March 2026, the elevator modernization project was the largest in Otis' history.


The Willis Tower project replaced the building's two Skydeck™ elevators and their steel rails traveling 105 stories, modernized 83 elevators - including replacing the machines for all of them - and installed 10 new elevators and six escalators.


The project presented significant logistical and engineering challenges. At least nine elevators were out of service at any given time, with the machines distributed across more than 40 machine rooms throughout the building. With no option to use a crane to move heavy machinery, existing machines had to be disassembled for removal, and new machines were brought in as smaller components for assembly on site.


In total, the Otis team installed 362,921 feet, or 68.7 miles, of rope and 865,672 pounds, nearly 433 tons, of elevator machines over the course of this project.


The Otis Compass® 360 destination dispatch system features customized kiosk interfaces and connects all passenger elevators into one centralized dispatching network. This is significantly more complex than in most high-rise buildings, intelligently and efficiently coordinating elevator traffic to move passengers through the building. The result is a smoother, more seamless passenger experience.


Otis also implemented its Otis ONE™ IoT service platform* at Willis Tower, providing real-time performance insights and system monitoring for maintenance and operations teams.


The building remained occupied by tenants and continued welcoming millions of visitors as work progressed, requiring careful phasing and project management, close stakeholder coordination and continuous attention to passenger flow.


Otis continues to care for the Willis Tower, providing service for the more than 100 elevator and escalator units in the building.


**Why Shanghai Science and Technology Museum won Escalator Modernization of the Year**


Smart technology, data, and continuous improvement guided Otis' modernization of the vertical mobility solutions.


The Shanghai Science and Technology Museum is often cited among China's top-tier national museums, drawing millions of visitors every year from China and abroad. The museum closed its doors in 2023 for a RMB 8.2 billion ($1.2 billion) renovation and reimagining of a science and technology museum for the digital age.


Otis was a key part of the museum's upgrade, delivering an improved visitor experience at this national public science and education hub, which reopened in January 2026.


Bringing the museum's bold, high-tech vision to life required the installation of seven modernized Otis Gen3™ elevator systems and the modernization of nine escalators which had been in place for more than 20 years.


Otis' escalator modernization approach retained the existing trusses, an important advantage to the customer. By preserving the existing truss and upgrading it with new components and technology, Otis helped reduce downtime and disruption.


The[Otis 520 NPE escalators](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4830168-1&h=1909911728&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.otis.com%2Fen%2Fus%2Fproducts-services%2Fproducts%2Fescalators-and-moving-walks%2Fpublic-escalator&a=Otis+520+NPE+escalators) are engineered to handle high passenger volumes. Three have bespoke glass side panels that expose the mechanisms to visitors – helping bring STEM education to life as a working exhibit. Construction tolerances had to be precise because the structure would be fully seen. The exposed equipment also requires specific maintenance practices to keep the internal mechanical structure clean and visible.


With a high-performance motor, passenger-sensing sleep mode, and intelligent lubrication, the system is designed to achieve an A+++ energy performance rating based on ISO25745-3:2015.


Otis now provides ongoing maintenance services for the elevators and escalators to support safe mobility for the museum's millions of visitors every year, with digital technology and predictive maintenance keeping everything running smoothly.


Learn more about Otis major projects and modernizations at the[Otis Global Projects page](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4830168-1&h=2573337168&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.otis.com%2Fen%2Fcompany%2Findustries-projects%2Fotis-global-projects&a=Otis+Global+Projects+page) .


*Otis ONE features are subject to a maintenance contract and paid tiered subscription with Otis.


**About Otis**


Otis gives people freedom to connect and thrive in a taller, faster, smarter world. The global leader in the manufacture, installation, service and modernization of elevators and escalators, we move 2.5 billion people a day and maintain approximately 2.5 million customer units worldwide – the industry's largest Service portfolio. You'll find us in the world's most iconic structures, as well as residential and commercial buildings, transportation hubs and everywhere people are on the move. Headquartered in Connecticut, USA, Otis is 72,000 people strong, including 45,000 field professionals, all committed to manufacturing, installing and maintaining products to meet the diverse needs of our customers and passengers in more than 200 countries and territories.
